text: Verified by Greg Tomasik on January 24, 2022 Greg is the co-founder of GermanTechJobs.de. Greg is the co-founder of GermanTechJobs.de. This guide helps you find a job in Berlin, from finding job listings to your first day at work.

title: Salaries in Germany
text: Know how much you should earn, and how much taxes you will pay. This helps you negotiate a better salary.

title: Permission to work
text: You might need a National Visa or residence permit to work in Germany. It can take a few months to get. When you change jobs, you might need to apply for a new residence permit. Who needs a residence permit?

title: Language
text: You don’t need to speak German to find a job, but it really helps. English-speaking jobs are harder to find. Most companies prefer German speakers. You can find English-speaking jobs in… Tech companies Delivery services like Lieferando, Wolt and Flink Customer service and call centres Restaurants, cafes and bars Companies with English-speaking offices Au pair families You can teach English in Germany, but you need qualification, it’s hard to find work, and the pay is bad.

text: Indeed.com – Job search engine. You can filter by language and set alerts. LinkedIn – Networking website with a big jobs section. Very popular. ArbeitNow – Job listing website. Made in Berlin. Jobted Xing – Similar to LinkedIn. You can’t filter by language. Glassdoor – Company reviews, salary reports and job listings. You need an account.

title: German resumes
text: German CVs are longer than American resumes. They include your date of birth, your citizenship and a photo of you. You should go to a photo studio and get a professional portrait for your resume. A career coach can help you write a better resume. Useful links: How to write a German resume – HalloGermany German resume examples – Imagine foundation Resume checklist – Imagine foundation Lingoking – Translate your resume to German

title: Cover letters
text: Include a short cover letter ( Anschreiben) with your application. It’s a personal introduction. It explains who you are, what you do, why you apply for this job, and why they should hire you. Don’t send the same cover letter to everyone. Do your research, and personalise the letter for each job offer. Keep it short and easy to read. Get feedback from other people before you send it. A career coach can help you write better cover letters. How to write a German cover letter – HalloGermany Advice for cover letters with examples – Hacker News

In Germany, the interview process is very long. It can take a few weeks, and even a few months. You might have multiple interviews with different people. It depends on the company and the job. You need a lot of time for this.

title: The phone screen
text: The interview process starts with a short call. A recruiter or hiring manager will ask you a few questions. They will try to understand who you are, what you want, and how you fit the job offer. It’s a simple check before they invite you for an interview. How to prepare – Imagine Foundation

title: The technical interview
text: Most tech companies have technical interviews or coding challenges. They verify that you know how to do your job. Technical interviews are different at every company. They might ask you technical questions, ask you to solve a problem during the interview, or complete a technical challenge at home. Some companies don’t have technical interviews.

title: Meet the team
text: Most companies have a team interview. You meet your future team to see if you work well together. This interview is more relaxed. You might just talk with the team, or have lunch together.
After your interview, the company can make a job offer.

title: Salary negotiation
text: After you get the job offer, you can negotiate a better salary. You can also ask for things like a relocation bonus or more vacation days. Salaries in Germany

title: The job contract
text: Read your job contract carefully. If your employer promised something to you during the interview, verify that it’s in your contract. Only sign the contract if you agree with everything. Send the signed contract by email or by post. If you are not sure about your contract, ask for help or talk to a lawyer.

If you are not a citizen of the EU, EEA or Switzerland, you need a residence permit to live in Germany. Sometimes, you must wait for your residence permit to start working. It takes 3 to 6 months to get a new residence permit. How to get a residence permit If you already have a residence permit, you might need the Ausländerbehörde ’s permission to change jobs. Sometimes, you can start your new job immediately. How to change jobs

title: Things your employer needs
text: During your first month at a new company, your employer needs a few things: Your bank account Your employer will pay you by bank transfer. Any European bank account should work. Your tax ID ( Steueridentifikationsnummer) You get it when you register your address for the first time. If you can’t register your address, you can still get a tax ID. Your social insurance number ( Sozialversicherungsnummer) If you have public health insurance, you get this number automatically in the mail. If you have private health insurance, you must apply for it. Your insurance broker can do it for you. Your employer can sometimes do it for you. Your health insurance number ( Krankenversicherungsnummer) You get it 2 to 7 days after you choose health insurance. Your employer needs this number to take health insurance payments from your salary. Your employer can choose health insurance for you, but it’s a bad idea. Ask my broker to help you choose, it’s free. You can start working without these things. Your employer can’t require an address registration certificate.

title: Things you must know
text: In Germany, most people are paid once per month. You usually get paid on the 1st or 15th day of the month. You get your first paycheck 30 to 45 days after you start working. You usually get paid by bank transfer. Most employees in Germany are paid by bank transfer once per month, on the first day of the month. [§ 614 BGB] Your employer takes wage tax, health insurance, pension insurance and unemployment insurance from your paycheck. Income tax calculator How taxes work During your first 6 months at a new company, you are in your probation period ( Probezeit). During that time, it’s easier to get fired. It’s also harder to find an apartment, because you don’t have a stable job. How the probation period works All employees in Germany get paid vacation days, and paid sick leave. You don’t work on public holidays, but you still get paid. How to take vacations What to do when you are sick

Most of your job search costs are tax-deductible: Relocation costs If you move closer to your new job, you can deduct your moving costs. Job search costs Coaching, resume writing, professional photos, translations, printing costs, job search services… Travel costs Fuel, train tickets, hotels, meals and parking fees to go to job interviews. Immigration costs Work-related immigration costs are tax-deductible. For example, Blue Card or work visa application fees. If you started working in the middle of the year, you probably paid too much wage tax. Make a tax declaration to lower your income tax, and get some money back.

title: Career coaching
text: These people can help you get hired. For example, they can review your resume and cover letter. Their fee is tax-deductible. Imagine Foundation – Free career coaching for software engineers and data scientists Hallo Germany – Career coaching
